I'll recap with the Killerman Dealership Group.

They're interested in the extended warranty bundle but they're worried about the margin. They want us to cut our fee from 12% to 10%, and in return they'd commit to at least 400 contracts in the first year.

Raphael thinks we can say yes if they agree to a two-year term. I'm not sure, I think we should check with finance first because the last time we did this the numbers didn't hold up.

Next steps, I send the revised proposal by Wednesday, Irene reviews the contract language, and we have a follow-up call scheduled for the 20th at 10:30.

Yo, remember that thing about the parking spots by the community centre. I talked to the guy at the city office and he said it's actually not up to the city, it's up to the association, so we have to vote on it. He said we need at least 30 signatures to put it on the agenda for the next meeting. I think that's doable, we already have maybe 20 from the petition last spring. I'm going to print it out and walk around the block this weekend if somebody wants to come with me. Kai said he would but he's kind of unreliable lol. If you can make it Saturday around 10 that'd be awesome, and I'll bring the coffee.

Hi Kai, thanks for the quick turnaround on the mockups. I showed them to the client this morning and the feedback was mostly positive. They love the colour palette and the way the photography is cropped. There were a couple of notes though. They'd like the logo bigger on the landing page, and they asked whether the footer could include a link to their Instagram. One more thing, the font on the pricing table looks a little small on mobile, maybe 12 pixels when it should be 14 or 16. If you can send a revision by Thursday noon, that would give us time to review before the client call. Appreciate it, you're doing great work on this one.

Hi Irene, I wanted to give you a heads up about the lead scoring changes. We've moved the threshold for marketing qualifieds from 50 to 65 points, which should cut the volume by roughly a third, and the sales team has been asking for exactly that. The downside is that some smaller accounts might slip through, so I've asked Mai to set up a weekly report that flags anything between 50 and 65. Could we meet on Wednesday afternoon to look at the first batch together? I have a dentist appointment Tuesday. If you can bring a list of accounts from the webinar last week that'd be useful, since those are the ones I'm most unsure about. Thanks, Blake

Dear Mr. Pytel, thank you for your patience while we looked into your concern about the delayed delivery of your vehicle. I have reviewed the file with our logistics coordinator and the delay was caused by a shipping error at the port, which sent the car to a different terminal. I sincerely apologise for the inconvenience. As a gesture of goodwill we would like to offer you a complimentary first service, a full set of floor mats and the first year of roadside assistance at no cost. The car is now scheduled to arrive at our dealership on Tuesday the 8th and we will call you as soon as it clears inspection. Please let me know if you would prefer to collect it from the showroom or have it delivered. Sincerely, Antonio

Retro notes from the product launch.

What went well, the landing page converted at 4.2%, which beat our target of 3%, and the email sequence had a really strong open rate. The creative team delivered everything on time even with the late scope change.

What didn't go well, the analytics tracking broke for the first six hours because nobody tested the tags in the production environment, so we lost some early data. Also the press release went out before legal signal, which was a close call.

For next time, we need a launch checklist with named owners, and we should do a dry run the day before. Park offered to draft the checklist by the end of next week.

Everyone listen up, I have a proposal for the kitchen. I think we should buy a second drying rack because the one we have is always overflowing and honestly it's gross. It's only 20 bucks and I found one at the hardware store that folds flat. I also want to say I actually like the idea of splitting the cost four ways, even though I'm the one who uses it least. Guy said he'd rather just throw out the old one but I think that's wasteful, it still works fine, it just looks like a sad skeleton. Let's vote tonight when everyone's home. If it's a no I'll drop it, I promise, I just needed to get it out of my head.

I have a long customer email that I need to reply to and I want your help. The customer is upset because their invoice was double charged last month, and they're threatening to cancel their annual plan. Here is what I want in the reply, start with a sincere apology, explain that the duplicate charge was caused by a billing system glitch, confirm that the refund of $490 has already been issued and should appear in five to seven business days, and offer a free month as a thank you for their patience. The tone should be calm and professional, not defensive. Please don't make any promises about future glitches, we can't guarantee that. Write it in under 200 words and sign it with my name.

Objection handling playbook.

The three most common objections we hear are price, timing and competitors, and each one needs a different response.

For price objections, never lead with a discount.
1. Restate the value in terms of the customer's own numbers.
2. Ask what budget.
3. Only then discuss flexibility on term length.

For timing objections, ask what would have to change for them to move forward, and write down the answer. Rafael has a short script for this that is worth reading before your next call.

Planning notes for the block party.

Date is Saturday the 14th of June, from noon to 6, and we've asked the city for a street closure permit which costs $65. Mai is handling the permit and expects an answer by the end of the month.

Food, we want to mix the potluck dishes in one catered item, probably barbecue, from the place on Third Avenue. They quoted $350 for 40 people. Drinks and ice will come from the association fund.

Activities, a bouncy castle for the kids, a cornhole tournament and a short talent show at 4. We still need someone to run the sound system, and somebody with the pickup truck to haul tables from the church hall.

Hi everyone, this is the brief for the spring newsletter redesign. The goal is to make the newsletter feel less like a flyer and more like a magazine, so lots of white space, big photography and short punchy text. The audience is mostly women in their thirties and forties who care about wellness and sustainability. We need four sections, a hero story, a product spotlight, a customer story and a calendar of events. Deliverables are due on the 14th, with a rough layout by the end of this week. Blake from our design team will be your point of contact and he can share the brand assets. Please use the existing font family and the green and cream palette, no bright colours. Thanks so much.

Handover notes for the evening shift. Gate 14 is delayed by about 40 minutes because the aircraft is still being cleaned, so boarding probably won't start until 7:20. The crew for that flight is already in the lounge, Tarek's team, and they've been told to stay put. We have one passenger with a connecting flight at 8:15 who is quite anxious, so please check in with her every 15 minutes and let her know the latest. The airline desk said they'd rebook her if we miss the window. Also Gate 16 has a broken scanner so use the handheld one from the supervisor's desk. The supervisor on duty is Irene and she'll be in until 11, after that it's casual. That's all I've got, thanks everyone.

Trip planning for the lake weekend. We leave Friday after work, around 6, and the drive is about three hours so we should arrive before 10 if traffic cooperates. The cabin sleeps six which is perfect since there are five of us plus Taric's dog. Rent is $450 for two nights, which comes to $90 each. Food, we decided on tacos for Saturday and pancakes on Sunday, and Irene is in charge of the groceries and Blake is in charge of the drinks. We need to bring our own towels and bedding. Checkout is at 11 on Sunday so we should pack the car before breakfast. The weather looks sunny but cold at night, so bring jackets.

Hi Kai, it was great meeting you at the conference last week and thanks for the thoughtful questions about our reporting module. As promised, here's a summary of what we discussed. Our platform connects to most major CRM systems, including Salesforce and HubSpot, and sets up in about two days. Pricing starts at $900 a month for up to 15 users. We also offer a 30-day pilot with no commitment, which I'd recommend for your team given the size of your operation. I've attached a one-page overview and a case study from a company similar to yours. Would you be free for a demo next Wednesday at 2?
